info.title: BrowserOS server API
info.description:
The contract between the BrowserOS extension and its local server. Generated from the server's Rust handlers and wire types; do not edit by hand.

Trust model, for every route except the `system` tag: the server binds `127.0.0.1` only; the `Host` header must name loopback; a request that carries an `Origin` header must carry the extension's origin (or one listed in `BROWSEROS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`); a request with no `Origin` may only use `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`. A refused request gets `403 {"error":"Forbidden"}`. A preflight `OPTIONS` from an allowed origin is answered by the trust layer itself (`204`, methods `GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS`, headers `Content-Type, Accept`).

Times are epoch milliseconds. Ids are strings.

Start one turn and stream it.
post.description:
Starts a server-owned run for the conversation and returns a subscriber view of it. Closing
this response does not stop the run; `stopTurn` does. A turn that cannot run (unknown
provider, no provider selected, not signed in, an agent that will not start) is a `200`
stream whose last chunk is `error`; only a body that does not parse is a `400`. The body is
the AI SDK UI message stream v1 for `ai@7.0.114`: each event is `data: <UiMessageChunk>`,
and the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`.

200.description: The run's chunks from the first one, then live.

409.description: A turn is already running for this conversation.

post.summary: One tiny model call to prove a provider works.
post.description:
A blank credential is filled from the stored row named by `providerId`, and only from a row
of the same provider type; when one is borrowed, the stored base URL, resource name and
region are forced too, so a saved secret is never sent to an address the caller chose. Every
`200` and `400` of this route is `{success, message, responseTime?}`, a body that does not
parse included, because the extension reads that one shape at any status.

post.summary: Ask an agent which models and reasoning levels it offers.
post.description:
Starts the agent's adapter, reads what it advertises, and stops it. It does not prove the
agent is signed in. A probe that cannot run answers 200 with `error` set and the defaults
`models: []`, `reasoning: null`, `supportsConfigOption: false`, `agentInfo: null`,
`protocolVersion: 0`; the dialog still lets the agent be created. (The old server answered
such a probe with `500 {error: {code, message}}`; the dialog renders either.)

Opens the callback listener on `127.0.0.1:1455` for as long as a sign-in is pending and
redirects to OpenAI's authorize page. The extension follows the redirect and opens the final
URL in a tab.

AgentProbe.description: What a coding agent advertised. A probe that could not run has `error` set.

ApiError.description: `{"error": "<one sentence>"}`: every refusal outside the chat path.

details.description: Upstream text with secrets scrubbed, at most 20,000 characters.

ChatErrorEnvelope.description:
The chat path's error body: the same envelope an `error` chunk carries in `errorText`, so
the chat error card renders both the same way.

ChatRequest.description:
One turn. The server owns history: the client sends the new message and the conversation
id, never the transcript. Unknown fields are ignored, because the extension and the server
update separately.

conversationId.description: Made by the extension. Keys the run, the stored row and the agent session.

message.description: The user's text for this turn.

userMessageId.description:
The id the client gave this user message. If the stored transcript already holds a
message with this id, everything after it is dropped and it is answered again: this is
how Retry and a repeated POST avoid storing the question twice. Absent: the server makes
an id and appends.

mode.description: `chat` gives the agent read-only access to the browser.

userWorkingDir.description: Working directory for a coding agent. Ignored for LLM targets.

supportsReasoning.description: From the extension's model catalogue. False turns reasoning options off.

persist.description: False in an incognito window: nothing is written, for either kind of target.

previousConversation.description: Text-only history, sent only when `persist` is false.

attachments.description: Files attached to this message. Coding agents only.

oneOf.description: The server's own agent loop on one of the user's LLM providers.

providerId.description: A provider row id. Absent means the selected provider.

ChatTarget.description:
What the turn talks to: the server's own loop on an LLM provider (`browseros`), or a coding
agent run through acpx.

ConversationDetail.description: A conversation summary with its transcript.

lastUserMessage.description: First 200 characters of the last user text.

targetType.description: `browseros`, `claude`, `codex`, or `custom` on rows from the old server.

ConversationTargetType.description: The kinds of target a stored conversation can name.

DefaultProvider.description: The selected row, or `null` when none is selected.

cdpConnected.description:
Whether the browser engine is linked to the browser. Always false where the engine is
not built.

autoOpenId.description: Set once for a tab the agent opened; tells the extension to open its panel there.

PanelAssignments.description: One event of `GET /chat/panels`: the whole table.

Provider.description:
A row of the `providers` table without its four secrets. Every key is always present;
nullable ones are `null` (the extension's converter reads the keys).

type.description: A ProviderType for `llm` rows, an AgentType for `acp` rows.

ProviderInput.description:
`PUT /providers/{providerId}`. A credential that is absent or an empty string keeps the
stored value; `null` clears it. Any other nullable field: absent keeps, `null` clears.

contextWindow.description: Tokens. A number, stored rounded (the old server validated a number).

headers.description: A value may contain the literal `{{conversationId}}`.

ProviderType.description: The provider types this server runs. Derived from `store::ProviderKind`, the one list.

RunState.description:
While `status` is `running`, `messages` ends with this turn's user message and the stream
supplies the answer. Once the run ends, `messages` contains the whole transcript, including
any sealed answer.

SignInStatus.description: Whether tokens are stored for this install.

can_update.description: Snake case because the browser's C++ reads this key.

StatusOk.description: Always `ok`: an answer at all is the signal.

Tab.description: A browser tab by the browser's own id.

TestProviderRequest.description:
`POST /test-provider`. A blank credential is filled from the stored row named by
`providerId`; when it is, the stored base URL and region are forced too, so a saved secret
is never sent to an address the caller chose. Unknown fields are ignored.

providerId.description: A saved row to borrow blank credentials from.

UiMessage.description:
An AI SDK `UIMessage` (`ai@7.0.114`). The extension passes it straight to `setMessages`, so
the part shapes are the SDK's, not ours; they are left open here on purpose.

oneOf.description:
First chunk. `messageId` is the server's id for the assistant message; it is the same in
the stored transcript and in every replay.
Around each model call of the loop. A coding-agent turn is one step.

A tool call exists. For the server's loop the tool is `run`; for a coding agent
`dynamic` and `providerExecuted` are true.
`errorText` is a JSON string holding a ChatErrorEnvelope, for both kinds of target.

UiMessageChunk.description:
The subset of the AI SDK `ai@7.0.114` UI message chunk union this server emits, one per
`data:` event of a chat stream. Field names and order rules are the SDK's; every chunk is
validated by the client and an unknown `type` fails the turn. `turn` serialises the real
chunks; this type only describes them for the contract.

UiPart.description: A part as the AI SDK stores it: its `type`, then that type's own fields.
